title: kbwho.py names the operator by a pseudonymous id read from the Claude login, and the session's role
goal: kbwho.py prints the operator's pseudonymous id, its source (inherited, auth-status, git or none) and the session's role (KB_ROLE, default interactive), with --json for tools; the id comes from KB_OPERATOR, else from the email key of claude auth status when that key is present, else from git config user.email; it is that email's alias in the uncommitted _private/operators.json, which kbwho writes as op- and 8 random hex digits on first use and an operator may edit; kbwho prints the email only with --show-email; kbwho.operator() gives other tools the same id and role; kb/_self/design.md's Teams and organizations section names kbwho as the source of the operator id that sessions, dispatched workers, backlog items, coord and commits record

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print("check failed:", e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import os, shutil, subprocess, tempfile, json, re
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
C = os.path.join(T, "clone")
shutil.copytree("_tools", os.path.join(C, "_tools"), ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", "*.pyc", "fixtures"))
shutil.copytree(".claude/hooks", os.path.join(C, ".claude", "hooks"))
for f in ("backlog.json", ".gitignore"):
    shutil.copy(f, C)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog"))
shutil.copy("kb/_self/map.csv", os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "map.csv"))
B = os.path.join(T, "bin"); os.makedirs(B)
EM = "jan.kowalski" + chr(64) + "corp-mail.test"  # built at run time: no address sits in the check's text
def stub(body):
    p = os.path.join(B, "claude"); open(p, "w").write("#!/bin/sh\n" + body + "\n"); os.chmod(p, 0o755)
stub("echo '{\"loggedIn\": true, \"authMethod\": \"claude.ai\", \"email\": \"%s\"}'" % EM)
ENV = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(("GIT_", "KB_", "CLAUDE"))}
ENV.update(PATH=os.pathsep.join([B, os.path.dirname(shutil.which("git")), "/usr/bin", "/bin"]), HOME=T,
           GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1", KB_LIVE_DOCS="0", KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(T, "coord.sqlite"),
           GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
def g(*a):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=C, env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
def run(tool, *a, stdin=None, **kw):
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(C, *tool.split("/")) if "/" in tool else os.path.join(C, "_tools", tool), *a],
                          cwd=C, env={**ENV, **kw}, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
g("init", "-q", "-b", "main"); g("add", "-A"); g("commit", "-qm", "base")
r = run("kbwho.py", "--json")
assert r.returncode == 0, ("kbwho.py --json fails", r.returncode, r.stderr[-300:])
d = json.loads(r.stdout)
assert d.get("source") == "auth-status" and d.get("role") == "interactive", ("not the login's identity and the interactive role", d)
assert re.fullmatch(r"op-[0-9a-f]{8}", d.get("id") or ""), ("the first id is not op- and 8 hex digits", d)
assert EM not in r.stdout and EM not in run("kbwho.py").stdout, "kbwho prints the email without --show-email"
assert EM in run("kbwho.py", "--show-email").stdout, "kbwho --show-email does not print the email"
M = os.path.join(C, "_private", "operators.json")
m = json.load(open(M))
assert m.get(EM) == d["id"], ("_private/operators.json does not map the email to its alias", m)
assert json.loads(run("kbwho.py", "--json").stdout)["id"] == d["id"], "the id changes between runs"
json.dump({EM: "jan-k"}, open(M, "w"))
assert json.loads(run("kbwho.py", "--json").stdout)["id"] == "jan-k", "an alias the operator set is not used"
d2 = json.loads(run("kbwho.py", "--json", KB_OPERATOR="op-orch0001", KB_ROLE="worker").stdout)
assert (d2.get("id"), d2.get("role"), d2.get("source")) == ("op-orch0001", "worker", "inherited"), ("the inherited identity is not used", d2)
stub("echo '{\"loggedIn\": false, \"authMethod\": \"none\"}'; exit 1")
G = os.path.join(T, "gitconfig"); open(G, "w").write("[user]\n\temail = ola" + chr(64) + "corp-mail.test\n")
d3 = json.loads(run("kbwho.py", "--json", GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=G).stdout)
assert d3.get("source") == "git" and d3.get("id") not in (None, "", "jan-k"), ("no fallback to git config user.email", d3)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(C, "_tools"))
os.environ.update(KB_OPERATOR="op-orch0001", KB_ROLE="orchestrator")
import kbwho
o = kbwho.operator()
assert (o.get("id"), o.get("role")) == ("op-orch0001", "orchestrator"), ("kbwho.operator() does not give the id and role", o)
assert not g("status", "--porcelain").strip(), ("kbwho left a file git would track", g("status", "--porcelain"))

gates.question: Where does kbwho read the operator's identity, and in which order? Facts: claude auth status documents only authMethod and configDirectory (public/claude/ci-and-headless.md:124, DOC S1824); its email key is undocumented, seen on 2.1.303 (ci-and-headless.md:126, UNK); no hook input, status line input or environment variable carries an email (ci-and-headless.md:127, DER).
options: KB_OPERATOR, then the email key of claude auth status when present, then git config user.email
only an alias the operator writes in _private/operators.json
gates.recommendation: KB_OPERATOR, then the email key of claude auth status when present, then git config user.email
gates.answer: KB_OPERATOR, then the email key of claude auth status when present, then git config user.email

gates.question: Which id stands for the operator in anything git tracks, coord events and exports? A plain hash of an email can be reversed by guessing the address; a random alias cannot.
options: an alias in _private/operators.json, written once as op- and 8 random hex digits and editable by the operator
the first 12 hex digits of the sha256 of the lowercased email
gates.recommendation: an alias in _private/operators.json, written once as op- and 8 random hex digits and editable by the operator
gates.answer: an alias in _private/operators.json, written once as op- and 8 random hex digits and editable by the operator
